solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Survey of a number of deliveries to struggle with (8)

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries (balls) from one bowler

annotation.surface: A cricket bowler battling through a long spell of overs.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sits on the cricket field; an over is the bowler's set of six balls, a staple of British crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name a broad look over a whole field rather than its details.

entries.clue: Army’s foremost youth turned up in charge of Germanic raiders (8)

annotation.definitionNote: an adjective: VANDALIC means 'of the Vandals'

indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down clue, turning a word up writes it bottom to top, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: the van (vanguard) is the front of an army
a lad is a youth; turned up it becomes DAL

annotation.surface: A young soldier at the front of an army taking command of barbarian invaders.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Army's foremost' looks like the first letter A; here it is the whole front of the army, the van.
annotation.definitionFit: The Vandals were a Germanic people who sacked Rome, so VANDALIC describes anything of those raiders.

entries.clue: Get together again concerning mounting chaos in island (10)

indicatorNotes.mounting: in a down clue, mounting climbs upward, so the letters read backwards
indicatorNotes.in: the chaos goes inside the island

blocks.note: Elba, Napoleon's island; MESS goes inside to give ELB(MESS)A, which read upward is ASSEMBLE

annotation.surface: A committee meeting again to discuss the turmoil spreading on an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mounting' applies to the whole of 'chaos in island', not just the chaos: build ELB(MESS)A first, then read it upward.
annotation.definitionFit: To reassemble is to gather together once more.

entries.clue: Devil back grabbing saint, one old one receiving help from angels (10)

indicatorNotes.grabbing: the back grabs the saint, holding S inside it

blocks.note: an imp is a little devil
the rear is the back; it grabs S to give RE(S)AR
I = one, the Roman numeral, then O = old, as in OT (Old Testament)

annotation.surface: A devilish story of a saint being seized, set against a picture of angels coming to help.
annotation.walkthrough: In the theatre an 'angel' is a backer who puts money into a show, so the angels help the producer, not a saint. 'Back' is a noun here, the rear, not a reversal instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An impresario stages shows, often funded by the private investors the theatre calls angels.

entries.clue: Factory work in town near Doncaster (7)

blocks.note: a works is a factory, as in gasworks

annotation.surface: A factory job in a northern English town.
annotation.walkthrough: Worksop is a market town in Nottinghamshire, a few miles south of Doncaster in South Yorkshire.
annotation.definitionFit: Worksop lies about fifteen miles south of Doncaster.

entries.clue: Not as much to be thankful for having lost billions (4)

indicatorNotes.having lost: a thing that has lost something no longer has it, so the word before has a letter taken away

blocks.note: to bless something is to be thankful for it, as in 'bless the rain'

annotation.surface: Someone with less to be grateful for after losing a fortune.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a rich man counting his blessings after a crash; the billions are only the letter B.
annotation.definitionFit: Less means a smaller amount, not as much.

entries.clue: What’s used in the studio of advanced artist (6)

annotation.surface: The equipment in the studio of a pioneering painter.
annotation.walkthrough: The artist's studio suggests easels and brushes; the studio meant is a photographic or TV one.
annotation.definitionFit: Cameras are the working tools of film, television and photographic studios.

entries.clue: Members of Balliol initially supporting gaudy meet for a purpose (5,3)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letters of 'Members of Balliol'
indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down clue, the supporter sits beneath: MOB goes under FLASH

blocks.note: the first letters of Members, Of, Balliol

annotation.surface: Oxford college men backing their college gaudy, a feast held for old members.
annotation.walkthrough: A gaudy is a reunion dinner at an Oxford college, so 'gaudy' looks like a noun; here it is the adjective, showy. Balliol is an Oxford college.
annotation.definitionFit: A flash mob is a crowd that gathers suddenly in a public place to perform something, then disperses.

entries.clue: Left prince accepting university examination (8)

indicatorNotes.accepting: the prince takes the university inside him

blocks.note: left over: 'is there any left?' = 'is there any over?'
Prince Hal, Shakespeare's young Henry V

annotation.surface: A prince who has departed, having been admitted to university after an exam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as departed; it is 'remaining', OVER.
annotation.definitionFit: An overhaul is a thorough examination, with repairs where needed.

entries.clue: Make a temporary stop using enclosed chart with motorway going east (6)

indicatorNotes.going east: in an across clue east is rightward: the M moves one place right through MAP

blocks.note: enc. = enclosed, the abbreviation at the foot of a letter
a chart is a MAP; its M (motorway) moves eastward past the A

annotation.surface: A driver breaking a journey, following the map included with the directions along the motorway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Motorway going east' reads as a road direction; it tells you to shift the M of MAP rightward.
annotation.definitionFit: To encamp is to set up camp, stopping somewhere for a while.

entries.clue: Abandonment of ski harness on the run (10)

annotation.surface: A skier's harness left behind on a downhill run.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abandonment' reads as leaving something behind; it means wild, unrestrained behaviour.
annotation.definitionFit: Abandon (or abandonment) is lack of restraint, which is rakishness.

entries.clue: Lead actor’s prompt about line (4)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the prompt is wrapped around the line's letter

blocks.note: a cue is the line prompting an actor to speak

annotation.surface: A star waiting in the wings for a prompt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead actor' sits together in the surface as the star; split it, and 'Lead' alone is the definition, the hint a detective follows.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the detective sense: a lead is a piece of information pointing toward the solution.

entries.clue: What’s triggered by burning cooked korma meals (5,5)

indicatorNotes.cooked: the letters are cooked up into a new order

annotation.surface: Curry left too long on the stove, setting off the alarm.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue tells the familiar kitchen story, and the answer is exactly what goes off in it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the device exists to go off when smoke from burning reaches it.

entries.clue: Tending to prove event Iliad misrepresented (10)

indicatorNotes.misrepresented: the letters are presented wrongly, rearranged

annotation.surface: A classicist arguing that Homer got the facts of the Trojan War wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests historical accuracy in Homer's epic; 'misrepresented' is only the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Evidential means providing evidence, tending to prove something.

entries.clue: Brown perhaps touches the earth before spring (10)

blocks.note: a caper is a leap, a spring

annotation.surface: A gardener kneeling on the soil before the growing season begins.
annotation.walkthrough: Capability Brown was the great 18th-century English landscape gardener; 'Brown' looks like a colour or a surname only.
annotation.definitionFit: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown designed the grounds of many English country houses, a landscaper by trade.

entries.clue: Ingredient of salad that’s cold in the main (7)

blocks.note: a crisp, pale-hearted lettuce variety used in salads
the main is poetic for the open sea; the cold thing floating there is a mass of ice

annotation.surface: A salad that is served chilled as a main course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the main' passes for 'mostly' or 'as a main course'; poetically the main is the ocean.
annotation.definitionFit: Iceberg is a crisp lettuce, and an iceberg is a cold mass of ice at sea.

entries.clue: Cruel, being puerile round unpleasant smell (8)

indicatorNotes.round: round means surrounding, so the puerile word encircles the smell

blocks.note: a hum is informal British for a bad smell

annotation.surface: Childish bullying involving a nasty smell.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'hum' is informal British for a stink, as in 'there's a hum in here'. 'Being' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Inhumane means lacking compassion, cruel.

entries.clue: Youngster born under Leo? (4,3)

blocks.note: the surface reading: a child born under the star sign Leo, late July to late August
the setter's reading: Leo is Latin for lion, so a young one 'born under' a real lion is its offspring

annotation.surface: A child whose birthday falls in the star sign Leo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Born under Leo' is astrology talk for a late-summer birthday; take it literally and the young one is born beneath an actual lion.
annotation.definitionFit: Leo is Latin for lion, so read literally the young one born beneath a lion is its offspring.

entries.clue: Creation of educational poetry? (8)

annotation.surface: Writing verse that teaches a lesson.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Creation' is meant in the sense of everything that exists, not something someone has made.
annotation.definitionFit: Creation, meaning all created things, is the universe.

entries.clue: Heavily-set man, soldier keeping men all back (7)

indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep is to hold, so the soldier holds the men inside him
indicatorNotes.back: back means in reverse, so 'all' is written from its end to its start

blocks.note: OR = other ranks, ordinary soldiers; inside GI: G(OR)I

annotation.surface: A burly squaddie holding his whole unit in reserve.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Men all back' sounds like a retreat; 'men' is the container's contents and only 'all' is reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: Gorilla is slang for a big, heavily built man, often a bodyguard or thug.

entries.clue: Formerly present until late afternoon broadcast? (10)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: broadcast things are heard, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: here = present, as in answering a roll call
to = until, as in 'nine to five'
late afternoon is four o'clock; said aloud, FOUR is spelt FORE

annotation.surface: A radio programme that used to run until teatime.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Late afternoon' has to become a clock time, four, before the sound change gives FORE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, if a formal one: both mean 'before now'.

entries.clue: Perform ceremony outside Mecca regularly (6)

indicatorNotes.outside: outside means around, so the ceremony surrounds the other letters
indicatorNotes.regularly: regularly means at even intervals, so take every other letter: mEcCa gives EC

annotation.surface: Pilgrims carrying out a ritual beyond Mecca at set times.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perform ceremony' reads as one phrase, a priest officiating; the definition is only 'Perform', in the sense of reciting a poem.
annotation.definitionFit: To recite is to perform a piece aloud from memory.

entries.clue: Came out with it one day (4)

blocks.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, SA

annotation.surface: Someone who finally blurted out a secret one day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Came out with it' reads as a whole phrase for confessing, but 'it' belongs to the wordplay as SA, the 1920s 'It girl' kind of sex appeal.
annotation.definitionFit: To come out with something is to say it.

entries.clue: Expert in smut, say, mostly I go dancing around clubs (10)

indicatorNotes.dancing: the letters dance into a new order
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go around C

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters; 'mostly' is fodder, not an instruction

annotation.surface: A prude confessing a weakness for dirty jokes while dancing round nightclubs.
annotation.walkthrough: Smut is a fungal disease of cereal crops, so its expert studies fungi. 'Mostly' looks like an instruction to shorten something, but it is fodder; the anagram MYOLOGIST takes C after its MY.
annotation.definitionFit: A mycologist studies fungi, and smut is a fungus that attacks grain.

entries.clue: Warning females to lose weight (4)

indicatorNotes.to lose: to lose something is to be left without it, so the letter for weight drops out of the word

annotation.surface: A health warning telling women to slim down.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a diet lecture; the weight lost is only the letter W.
annotation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign warning of what is to come.

entries.clue: I am left message (6)

blocks.note: port = the left side of a ship

annotation.surface: Someone telling you they have left you a message.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the surface as 'I am left a message'; 'message' means meaning, the import of something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the import of words is their meaning or significance, the message they carry.

entries.clue: Case of intolerable situation for teacher’s union? (8)

blocks.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers; NUT's = NUTS

annotation.surface: A union's grievance case about teachers' unbearable working conditions.
annotation.walkthrough: The NUT was the main British teachers' union. 'Case' is a casing: a nutshell encases a nut.
annotation.definitionFit: A nutshell is the hard case around a nut.

entries.clue: One may react against this chap of greater stature stripped (8)

indicatorNotes.stripped: stripped of its outer layer, the first and last letters go

blocks.note: a man who is taller is a TALLER GENT; stripping peels off the outside letters

annotation.surface: A shorter man bristling against a bigger fellow who has taken his shirt off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stripped' suggests undressing; here TALLER GENT loses its outer T at each end. The definition is the whole first half, before 'this'.
annotation.definitionFit: An allergen is a substance that the body reacts against.
